clue.text: Inferior progressive school, now defunct

parts.note: secondary means lesser, of lower rank
progressive ideas are modern ones

explanation.surface: A sneer at a second-rate trendy school that has since closed down.
explanation.walkthrough: A secondary modern was the British state school for pupils who failed the eleven-plus exam; most were replaced by comprehensives from the 1960s on.
explanation.definitionFit: Secondary moderns were a kind of British state school, largely abolished decades ago, so the type is now defunct.

clue.text: Chapters consisting of half-finished letters and poems

indicators.note: only half the word is finished, so its second half is dropped

parts.note: epistles are letters, as in the New Testament
odes are lyric poems

explanation.surface: A book whose chapters are made of unfinished letters and poems, like a scrapbook novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are EPISTLES, an eight-letter word; keep its first four.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodes are instalments or sections of a story, so they can stand for chapters.

clue.text: Wild, bare Scottish hillside

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the word's letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a windswept, treeless slope in the Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Brae is the Scots word for a hillside or steep bank.

clue.text: Finished houses are made pleasing

indicators.note: a word that houses another holds it inside like a building

parts.note: finished means ended
taken as written

explanation.surface: Completed homes have been made attractive to buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Houses' reads as a plural noun next to 'Finished', but it is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone liked, so endeared means rendered pleasing or dear to others.

clue.text: Decline in the Dow or Sensex

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters that follows, spanning the word boundary

parts.note: the letters straddle dOW OR SENsex

explanation.surface: A market report about a fall in New York's and Mumbai's stock indices.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dow Jones and the Sensex are the share indices of New York and Mumbai.
explanation.definitionFit: To worsen is to get worse, a synonym of decline as a verb.

clue.text: Voluntary unit captured by irregular platoon

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor
irregular means not in proper order, so the soldiers' word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: A volunteer squad is taken prisoner by a band of irregular soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something voluntary is left to choice rather than required, which is what optional means.

clue.text: In the north the game is supported by many and is commonplace

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported means something else stands underneath

parts.note: in northern English dialect 'the' is shortened to t'
RU is rugby union
taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: Up north, a sport loved by the masses is ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire and Lancashire speech clips 'the' to t', as in 'down t' pit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A truism is a statement so obvious it is trite, a commonplace remark.

clue.text: Cupboards full of underwear?

parts.note: surface reading: storage crammed with knickers
setter's reading: drawers is an old word for knickers, and also the sliding boxes in bedroom furniture

explanation.surface: Someone's wardrobe is stuffed with nothing but knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is on drawers: underpants, and sliding compartments.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedroom storage cabinets with sliding compartments, which can literally hold drawers in the underwear sense.

clue.text: Translate Parsee books and letter into new language

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so the letters change their order

parts.note: taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
a letter of the alphabet, here O

explanation.surface: An instruction to render Zoroastrian scriptures into a modern tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: A Parsee is an Indian Zoroastrian; 'letter' can be any one letter, and the leftovers here demand O.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented language created in 1887, so it was a new language rather than an evolved one.

clue.text: Rod is an old unit of measurement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bar or pole for a bird to sit on
second meaning: an old length of five and a half yards

explanation.surface: A schoolbook fact: the rod was a historic measure of length.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod, pole and perch were all names for the same old length, so the surface is a true statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch is a bar a bird stands on, and also a former imperial unit equal to a rod or pole.

clue.text: Disgusting old boy's display of unseemly behaviour

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil
making a scene is an embarrassing public outburst

explanation.surface: Disapproval of a former pupil's loutish public behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Old boy is British for a former pupil of a school; the possessive 's only smooths the surface and adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive to decency, repugnant, a strong synonym for disgusting.

clue.text: Speaks contemptuously about Irish whiskies?

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to spit words is to say them with scorn
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at whiskey from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that whiskies are just one example of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits are distilled alcoholic drinks, of which whiskies are one example.

clue.text: Old bird's odd, misshapen egg

indicators.note: misshapen means put out of form, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
an egg is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A prehistoric bird laid a strange, deformed egg.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo was a flightless bird of Mauritius, extinct since the 1600s, so it is literally an old bird.

clue.text: Makes Mark call partner

indicators.note: to partner is to pair up, so the two words stand side by side

parts.note: a brand is a mark burned on livestock
to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: An instruction: get Mark to phone his other half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name and 'Makes' like a verb; Makes is a plural noun, as in makes of car.
explanation.definitionFit: A make is the manufacturer's label on a product, so makes are brand names.

clue.text: Citizen Kane's enigmatic pronouncement bored us terribly

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the words are badly jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A film critic's grumble that the famously cryptic last word of Citizen Kane was tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosebud is the dying word of Charles Foster Kane, the mystery the 1941 film sets out to solve.

clue.text: Bangor sounds as if it might be a thriving place

parts.words: Bangor sounds as if it might be a thriving place
parts.note: surface reading: the Welsh city's name sounds prosperous
setter's reading: split it as Bang plus -or, and a bang is a loud noise, so Bangor is a noisy place by name

explanation.surface: A remark that the name of the Welsh city of Bangor suggests a lively, prosperous town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangor begins with a word for a loud explosive noise, and it is a town; put the two together and you have a phrase for a place enjoying rapid growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A place undergoing sudden economic growth and prosperity, typically after a gold rush or industrial surge.

clue.text: Manage tearaway

definitions.meaning: first meaning: succeed in doing something difficult
second meaning, read as 'tear away': remove by yanking

explanation.surface: An instruction to control an unruly youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: A tearaway is a reckless youth in British usage, but here the word splits as tear away.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull something off is to achieve it against the odds, and also to remove it by tugging it free.

clue.text: Place in which work united the common people

indicators.note: the first word is a place with something put in it, so it surrounds what follows

parts.note: taken as written
OP is short for opus, a work
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A location where united labour brought together ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like the definition, but it is the container; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: The populace is the general public, the ordinary people of a place.

clue.text: Left a bit of food, having a dental problem

parts.note: left over means remaining
a bite is a mouthful of food

explanation.surface: Someone couldn't finish their meal because of trouble with their teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: An overbite is a dental condition where the upper front teeth overlap the lower ones too far.

clue.text: Instrument with a lens and tiny compass

parts.note: micro means very small
compass in the sense of range or extent

explanation.surface: A list of kit: a magnifying device and a miniature compass.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass is not the navigation tool but range, as in 'within the compass of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A microscope is an optical device using lenses to magnify very small objects.

clue.text: Convincing man to support company

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporter stands below, so the man goes under the company

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a gent is a gentleman

explanation.surface: A persuasive argument for hiring someone to back up the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is forceful and persuasive, the same as a convincing one.

clue.text: Copper''s uncommon poison

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
rare means uncommon

explanation.surface: A detective story: the policeman's rare poison.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper reads as a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Curare is a plant-derived paralysing poison used on South American arrow tips.

clue.text: Broadcast old king's dirty grin

indicators.note: what is broadcast is heard, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's aged monarch

explanation.surface: A broadcast drama shows an aged monarch smirking lewdly.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is a lascivious or sly look, a smutty grin.

clue.text: Heavenly body troubles sailor

parts.note: to dog someone is to trouble or pursue them
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A celestial object causes problems for a seaman, perhaps by misleading his navigation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dog Star is Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, so it is a heavenly body.

clue.text: Now blog can be a weapon

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters may become something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that online writing can now be used to attack people.
explanation.definitionFit: The longbow is a tall bow for shooting arrows, the famous English weapon of medieval wars.

clue.text: Man named for refusal to take railway

indicators.note: taking on something means it is added on, so the second piece joins the first

parts.note: no is a refusal
EL is an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A man got his name because he would not ride the train.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a male given name, so it is a man's name.

clue.text: Frenchman and wife begin again

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A French husband and his wife make a fresh start.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to restart or resume something after a break, to begin it again.

clue.text: Kentish Town chap beloved by Jane

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cathedral city in Kent
second meaning: the brooding hero Jane Eyre loves in Charlotte Brontë's novel

explanation.surface: A man from the London district of Kentish Town is Jane's sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is a district of north London, but here it means a town in the county of Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester is a city on the Medway in Kent, and Mr Rochester is the man Jane Eyre marries.
